reference: "62.5 mg orally twice daily" for 4 weeks, then "increase to 125 mg orally twice daily after 4 weeks" (patients weighing more than 40 kg); "Patients >12 years of age and <40 kg: 62.5 mg twice daily". Contraindications: "Use of TRACLEER is contraindicated in females who are pregnant"; "concomitant use of TRACLEER and cyclosporine A is contraindicated"; "co-administration of glyburide and TRACLEER is contraindicated"; hypersensitivity.

question: A 54-year-old woman on sertraline 100 mg PO daily for depression, with no MAOI use in the past year, develops nasal congestion from an upper respiratory infection. She has no hypertension, coronary disease, arrhythmia, hyperthyroidism, diabetes or narrow-angle glaucoma, and is not pregnant. Her PCP recommends OTC pseudoephedrine.

reference: Directions, adults and children 12 years of age and over: take 2 tablets (30 mg each) "every 4-6 hours", not more than "4 doses in 24 hours". Warnings: "Do not use if you are now taking a prescription monoamine oxidase inhibitor (MAOI) (certain drugs for depression, psychiatric or emotional conditions, or Parkinson's disease), or for 2 weeks after stopping the MAOI drug."

question: A 46-year-old man in alcohol use disorder treatment has been abstinent for 6 months and is maintained on naltrexone 50 mg PO daily; he has never taken disulfiram. He develops symptomatic giardiasis confirmed by stool antigen testing. He has no nitroimidazole allergy and no Cockayne syndrome. His PCP prescribes oral tinidazole and counsels him to avoid alcohol during treatment and for 3 days afterwards.

reference: "Tinidazole is indicated for the treatment of giardiasis caused by Giardia duodenalis (also termed G. lamblia) in both adults and pediatric patients older than three years of age" ... "The recommended dose in adults is a single 2 g dose taken with food." Contraindications: hypersensitivity to tinidazole or other nitroimidazole derivatives, and Cockayne syndrome. (Parent premise mirror: metronidazole label — "Do not administer metronidazole to patients who have taken disulfiram within the last two weeks.")

question: A 38-year-old woman with chronic migraine on topiramate 50 mg PO BID for prophylaxis, taking no ergot derivative, develops symptomatic candidal esophagitis confirmed at endoscopy. She is not pregnant (negative pregnancy test), is HIV-negative, has normal hepatic and renal function, and takes no QT-prolonging medication. GI prescribes oral fluconazole.

reference: "Oral fluconazole, 200–400 mg (3–6 mg/kg) daily, for 14–21 days is recommended" (esophageal candidiasis, initial therapy).

question: A 68-year-old woman with HFrEF maintained on lisinopril 10 mg PO daily and furosemide 40 mg PO daily — no mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist, no amiodarone, ranolazine, simvastatin or other contraindicated CYP3A-sensitive drug — develops symptomatic COVID-19 with symptom onset 2 days ago. She is high-risk by age and cardiac disease, and her eGFR is 82 mL/min/1.73 m². PCP prescribes Paxlovid × 5 days.

reference: "300 mg nirmatrelvir (two 150 mg tablets) with 100 mg ritonavir (one 100 mg tablet), with all 3 tablets taken together twice daily for 5 days"; treatment should begin "as soon as possible after diagnosis of COVID-19 and within 5 days of symptom onset"; renal impairment: eGFR ≥60 to <90, no dose adjustment; eGFR ≥30 to <60, "150 mg nirmatrelvir (one 150 mg tablet) with 100 mg ritonavir (one 100 mg tablet) twice daily".

question: A 63-year-old woman with mild depression managed with cognitive behavioral therapy alone takes no prescription medications and no herbal supplements, including no St. John's wort. She is high-risk for severe COVID-19 by age and obesity, and develops symptomatic COVID-19 with symptom onset 3 days ago; her eGFR is 78 mL/min/1.73 m². PCP prescribes Paxlovid × 5 days.

reference: "300 mg nirmatrelvir (two 150 mg tablets) with 100 mg ritonavir (one 100 mg tablet), with all 3 tablets taken together twice daily for 5 days"; treatment must begin "within 5 days of symptom onset"; eGFR ≥60 to <90: no dose adjustment. Contraindicated concomitant drugs include "strong CYP3A inducers like rifampin and St. John's Wort".

question: A 64-year-old man with HFrEF on metoprolol succinate 50 mg PO daily — no ivabradine and no other CYP3A4-sensitive medication — develops moderate-to-severe oropharyngeal candidiasis after starting an inhaled corticosteroid. Renal and hepatic function are normal, electrolytes are normal, and he takes no other QT-prolonging drug. His PCP prescribes oral fluconazole.

reference: "For moderate to severe disease, oral fluconazole, 100–200 mg daily, for 7–14 days is recommended" (oropharyngeal candidiasis). Supporting the agent change: the current US ketoconazole tablet label states it is indicated only for "blastomycosis, coccidioidomycosis, histoplasmosis, chromomycosis, and paracoccidioidomycosis" in patients "who have failed or who are intolerant to other therapies", and it is not indicated for Candida infections.

question: A 24-year-old woman (BMI 22) presents 18 hours after a single episode of unprotected intercourse requesting emergency contraception. A urine pregnancy test is negative, she takes no enzyme-inducing medications, and she declines a copper IUD. PCP prescribes levonorgestrel (Plan B One-Step).

choices.C: 3 mg PO once (double dose for late presentation)
choices.D: 1.5 mg PO once, repeat in 24 hr

reference: 'take as soon as possible within 72 hours (3 days) after unprotected sex' — administered as one 1.5 mg tablet.

question: A 32-year-old woman presents with 4 days of painful visual loss in the right eye. Visual acuity is 20/200 on the right with a right relative afferent pupillary defect, red desaturation, and pain on eye movement; the left eye is normal. choices.D: 1 g IV once, then oral prednisone taper

question: A 68-year-old man had herpes zoster in the left T5 dermatome 5 months ago and has had continuous burning, allodynic pain in that dermatome ever since, currently 7/10 and disrupting sleep. Serum creatinine is 0.9 mg/dL with an estimated creatinine clearance above 60 mL/min. He was started on gabapentin 300 mg PO at bedtime on day 1 and tolerated 300 mg PO twice daily on day 2 with no sedation, dizziness or ataxia. His pain is unchanged. reference: 'Day 1: Single 300 mg dose; Day 2: 600 mg/day (i.e., 300 mg two times a day); Day 3: 900 mg/day (i.e., 300 mg three times a day)' and the dose 'can subsequently be titrated up as needed for pain relief to a dose of 1800 mg/day (600 mg three times a day).'

question: A 28-year-old woman (60 kg) ingested a reported 20 g of acetaminophen 6 hours ago in a suicide attempt. Her serum acetaminophen concentration drawn at 4 hours post-ingestion is 210 mcg/mL, above the Rumack-Matthew treatment line. ALT is 26, INR 1.0, and she is asymptomatic. She has no acetylcysteine allergy and no asthma. Toxicology initiates IV N-acetylcysteine.

choices.C: 150 mg/kg IV over 60 min, then 50 mg/kg × 4 hr, then 100 mg/kg × 16 hr

question: A 24-year-old woman at 22 weeks' gestation was a close household contact of a meningococcal disease case; the index patient was identified 18 hours ago. She is asymptomatic. She has no penicillin or cephalosporin allergy. Her PCP arranges chemoprophylaxis.

reference: Adult dosages: Rifampin '600 mg every 12 hrs' for '2 days'; Ciprofloxacin '500 mg' 'Single dose'; Ceftriaxone '250 mg' 'Single IM dose'. 'Ciprofloxacin is not generally recommended for persons aged <18 years or for pregnant and lactating women...' question: A 6-year-old boy (22 kg) has a venous blood lead level of 58 mcg/dL, confirmed on repeat venous testing. He is asymptomatic with no signs of encephalopathy and is tolerating oral intake. The lead paint source in his home has been abated and he is no longer living in the contaminated environment. Iron studies are normal. Toxicology initiates succimer.

question: A 13-month-old boy (9 kg) with SMA type 2 (bi-allelic SMN1 deletion, 3 copies of SMN2) has completed intrathecal nusinersen loading. His anti-AAV9 antibody titre is 1:25, baseline AST, ALT, bilirubin and platelet count are normal, and he has no active infection. Genetics proposes onasemnogene abeparvovec (Zolgensma) with the prescribed systemic corticosteroid course beginning the day before infusion.

reference: 'ZOLGENSMA is an adeno-associated virus (AAV) vector-based gene therapy indicated for the treatment of pediatric patients less than 2 years of age with spinal muscular atrophy (SMA) with bi-allelic mutations in the survival motor neuron 1 (SMN1) gene.' 'The recommended dose of ZOLGENSMA is 1.1 × 10^14 vector genomes per kilogram (vg/kg) of body weight.' 'Administer ZOLGENSMA as a single-dose intravenous infusion.'

question:
A 30-year-old woman with eclampsia (postpartum seizure) is on IV
magnesium sulfate 4 g loading + 2 g/hr infusion. Four hours in she
becomes somnolent; deep tendon reflexes are absent, respiratory rate
is 9/min with SpO2 92% on room air, and serum Mg is 11.4 mg/dL. Urine
output has been 15 mL/hr and creatinine is 1.6. The magnesium infusion
is stopped and oxygen is applied.

choices.D: Calcium gluconate 1 g IV once over 3-5 min

reference: IV calcium gluconate is the specific ANTIDOTE for magnesium toxicity — administered only when Mg toxicity is clinically manifest (respiratory depression, loss of DTRs, cardiac conduction issues). Scheduled prophylactic calcium during therapeutic-level magnesium infusion antagonizes magnesium's anti-seizure effect and precipitates recurrent seizure.

question:
A 22-year-old woman in DKA (presenting glucose 620, pH 7.15, anion gap
26) is on IV insulin 0.1 U/kg/hr with IV NS and potassium replacement
at 20 mEq/L. At hour 6 her glucose is 205 mg/dL but the anion gap is
still 18 with serum bicarbonate 14 and pH 7.29. Corrected serum sodium
is 142, potassium 4.0, and urine output is good. The team plans to
change the IV fluid so the insulin infusion can continue.

reference: Once the plasma glucose is ∼ 200 mg/dl, 5% dextrose should be added to replacement fluids to allow continued insulin administration until ketonemia is controlled while at the same time avoiding hypoglycemia. ... In general, 0.45% NaCl infused at 250-500 ml/h is appropriate if the corrected serum sodium is normal or elevated; 0.9% NaCl at a similar rate is appropriate if corrected serum sodium is low.

question:
A 22-year-old woman with subacute behavioral changes, seizures,
dyskinesia, and autonomic instability has CSF positive for anti-NMDA
receptor antibodies. Neurology has arranged pelvic MRI and ultrasound
for ovarian teratoma, has started IVIG 2 g/kg divided over 5 days, and
has plasma exchange available as an alternative. Infection has been
excluded, and she has no active tuberculosis, no uncontrolled diabetes,
and no systemic infection. Which corticosteroid regimen should
accompany the IVIG as first-line therapy?

reference: Anti-NMDA receptor encephalitis first-line treatment: high-dose IV methylprednisolone (1 g × 5 days) + IVIG (2 g/kg over 5 days) OR plasma exchange. Second-line (if no response): rituximab + cyclophosphamide. Tumor evaluation (teratoma removal) essential.

question: A 34-year-old woman with no drug allergies (she has tolerated amoxicillin previously) develops streptococcal pharyngitis confirmed by rapid antigen testing, with fever 39.1 C and marked tonsillar exudates. She is not pregnant and has normal renal function. PCP plans amoxicillin.

reference: Severe infections: "875 mg every 12 hours or 500 mg every 8 hours" ... "It is recommended that there be at least 10 days' treatment for any infection caused by Streptococcus pyogenes to prevent acute rheumatic fever."

question: A 74-year-old woman with severe postmenopausal osteoporosis (T-score -3.8) had hypocalcemia that has been corrected before therapy: ionized calcium 4.9 mg/dL (normal), 25-OH vitamin D 38 ng/mL, and she takes calcium 1000 mg plus vitamin D 800 IU daily. CrCl 62 mL/min. Endocrinology plans denosumab (Prolia).

"All patients should receive calcium 1000 mg daily and at least 400 IU vitamin D daily."

question: A 37-year-old woman with relapsed multiple myeloma has progressed after two prior regimens including lenalidomide and bortezomib. She is not pregnant (two negative pregnancy tests) and uses two forms of contraception per the POMALYST REMS. Hepatic and renal function are normal. Oncology initiates pomalidomide with dexamethasone.

reference: "The recommended dosage of POMALYST is 4 mg once daily orally with or without food on Days 1 through 21 of each 28-day cycle until disease progression."

question: A 44-year-old woman with newly diagnosed multiple myeloma is planned for thalidomide plus dexamethasone induction. reference: "200 mg once daily (in 28-day treatment cycles) orally with water, preferably at bedtime and at least 1 hour after the evening meal." Dexamethasone "40 mg daily administered orally on days 1-4, 9-12, and 17-20 every 28 days."

question: A 44-year-old woman with cryopyrin-associated periodic syndromes on rilonacept (320 mg SC loading, then 160 mg weekly) developed severe pyelonephritis six weeks ago. She completed a 14-day course of antibiotics, has been afebrile for 10 days, and repeat blood and urine cultures are sterile with WBC 7,100. Renal function is normal. question: A 61-year-old man with newly diagnosed Philadelphia chromosome-positive chronic myeloid leukaemia in chronic phase (no prior tyrosine kinase inhibitor) has a baseline QTc of 428 ms with normal potassium and magnesium, no long QT syndrome, and takes no other QT-prolonging or CYP3A4-interacting medication. question: A 66-year-old woman with HFrEF (EF 32%, NYHA class II) is in sinus rhythm with a resting heart rate of 78 bpm on maximally tolerated carvedilol 25 mg BID, plus an ACE inhibitor and a mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist. question: A 44-year-old woman on topiramate 50 mg PO BID for migraine prophylaxis develops symptomatic COVID-19 and presents on day 4 of symptoms. question: A 38-year-old woman on topiramate 50 mg PO BID for chronic migraine prophylaxis develops invasive pulmonary aspergillosis. question: A 44-year-old woman with moderate persistent asthma, a condition that places her at higher risk of influenza complications, was a household contact of a confirmed influenza A case 24 hours ago. question:

reference: the HCP should receive 1 dose of HBIG and 1 dose of HepB vaccine administered as soon as possible after the exposure. The HCP should complete the HepB vaccine series according to the vaccination schedule. ... The standard adult dose of HBIG is 0.06 mL/kg.

question: A 68-year-old woman (70 kg) was last known well 2 hr ago and has left-sided weakness with neglect; NIHSS is 12. Non-contrast CT shows no hemorrhage, no established hypodensity, and no mass effect, ASPECTS 9. CT angiography shows no large-vessel occlusion. BP 150/85, INR 1.0, no anticoagulant, no recent surgery. Neuro stroke team gives IV alteplase. Which regimen?

reference: The recommended dose is 0.9 mg/kg (not to exceed 90 mg total dose), with 10% of the total dose administered as an initial intravenous bolus over 1 minute and the remainder infused over 60 minutes.

question: A 24-year-old woman requests emergency contraception 3 days (72 hr) after a single act of unprotected intercourse. Urine pregnancy test is negative; she has no purulent cervicitis, no current chlamydial or gonococcal infection, no PID, and no distorted uterine cavity. Same-day insertion is available and she would like ongoing contraception. Gynecology offers copper IUD insertion. Which is the best option?

choices.B: Copper IUD in 24 hr with pre-medication
choices.C: Ulipristal 30 mg PO + copper IUD in 5 d

reference: The Cu-IUD may be placed within 5 days of the first act of unprotected sexual intercourse as emergency contraception. ... Cu-IUDs are highly effective as emergency contraception and can be continued as regular contraception.

question: A 58-year-old man (70 kg) presents to the ED with fever, headache, neck stiffness and confusion. LP is performed; CSF shows 4,200 WBC (92% neutrophils), glucose 18, protein 220, and Gram stain shows gram-positive diplococci. No antibiotics have yet been given. Neurology gives IV dexamethasone 10–20 min before the first dose of ceftriaxone + vancomycin. Which dexamethasone regimen is indicated?

reference: Dose: "0.15 mg/kg every 6 hours"; Duration: "2-4 days"; Timing: "10–20 min before, or at least concomitant with, the first dose of antimicrobial therapy."

question: A 58-year-old man presents 6 hr after sudden dyspnea and a syncopal episode. CTA confirms a saddle pulmonary embolism; BP is 76/44 after 1 L of crystalloid, HR 124, echo shows RV dilation with septal flattening, troponin elevated. No recent surgery, stroke, head trauma, intracranial disease, bleeding diathesis, or uncontrolled hypertension. IV unfractionated heparin has been started. Cardiology proposes systemic thrombolysis. Which regimen is indicated?

reference: "The recommended dose is 100 mg administered by IV infusion over 2 hours." Contraindications: "Active internal bleeding"; "Recent intracranial or intraspinal surgery or serious head trauma"; "Intracranial conditions that may increase the risk of bleeding"; "Bleeding diathesis"; "Current severe uncontrolled hypertension"; for PE also "History of recent stroke."

question: A 26-year-old Rh-negative woman at 10 wk gestation presents with vaginal bleeding that began 12 hr ago (threatened miscarriage; fetal cardiac activity present on ultrasound). Antibody screen is negative, so she is not already alloimmunized. She has not received anti-D immune globulin in this pregnancy. OB orders anti-D IG now. Which order is correct?

reference: "Actual or threatened termination of pregnancy (spontaneous or induced) up to and including 12 weeks gestation. Administer within 72 hours." ... administration "within 72 hours of suspected or proven exposure to Rh-positive red blood cells."

question: A 68-year-old woman collapses in the ED; the monitor shows ventricular fibrillation. High-quality CPR is in progress; she has received three defibrillation shocks and IV epinephrine, and VF persists. No antiarrhythmic has been given yet. The code team gives amiodarone as a rapid IV bolus. Which dose is indicated for this first antiarrhythmic dose?

reference: "initial IV/IO dose of 300 mg with a second IV/IO dose of 150 mg if required" — "Amiodarone or lidocaine may be considered for VF/pVT that is unresponsive to defibrillation" (Class IIb, LOE B-R).

question: A 34-year-old woman (45 kg) with bee-sting anaphylaxis (BP 78/48, bronchospasm, diffuse urticaria) receives IM epinephrine 0.3 mg mid-thigh, IV fluids, and H1/H2 blockers, with resolution of the hypotension and wheeze. Two hours into observation she reports a moderate headache and myalgias. She remains nauseated and is not tolerating oral intake. No liver disease; no acetaminophen in the preceding 24 hr. ED gives IV acetaminophen. Which dose is correct?

reference: "For adults weighing 50 kg or more: 1000 mg every 6 hours or 650 mg every 4 hours, with a maximum single dose of OFIRMEV of 1000 mg." "For adults weighing under 50 kg: 15 mg/kg every 6 hours or 12.5 mg/kg every 4 hours, with a maximum single dose of OFIRMEV of 15 mg/kg."

question: An 82-year-old man with no baseline cognitive impairment (no dementia, no parkinsonism, no visual hallucinations at baseline) is hospitalized for a UTI and develops hyperactive delirium with agitation, pulling at lines and striking staff. The infection is being treated and non-pharmacologic measures have failed; he is a danger to himself and staff. ECG shows QTc 420 ms; K and Mg are normal; he is on no other QT-prolonging drug. Team gives haloperidol. Which order is correct?

reference: "HALOPERIDOL INJECTION IS NOT APPROVED FOR INTRAVENOUS ADMINISTRATION." Intravenous use carries heightened risk of QT prolongation and Torsades de Pointes; the approved route is intramuscular only. Initial parenteral doses of "2–5 mg intramuscularly for moderately to very severe symptoms"; debilitated and geriatric patients "require lower doses and more gradual dosage adjustments." Boxed warning: "Elderly patients with dementia-related psychosis treated with antipsychotic drugs are at an increased risk of death."

question: A healthy 4-month-old infant with no personal history of intussusception, no severe combined immunodeficiency, and no prior hypersensitivity reaction presents for scheduled vaccines. He received his first RotaTeq dose at 2 months of age and tolerated it. He is afebrile and well. Pediatrics gives the second dose of the rotavirus series. Which order is correct?

reference: "Administer orally as a series of 3 doses starting at 6 to 12 weeks of age, with the subsequent doses administered at 4 to 10 week intervals. The third dose should not be given after 32 weeks of age." Each dose consists of "2 mL." Contraindications: "History of Severe Combined Immunodeficiency Disease (SCID)"; "History of intussusception"; "A demonstrated history of hypersensitivity to the vaccine or any component of the vaccine."

question: A 44-year-old woman with no thymus disorder (no thymoma, no myasthenia gravis, no thymectomy), immunocompetent, not pregnant and not breastfeeding, with no history of acute hypersensitivity to eggs, egg products or gelatin, plans travel to Amazonian Brazil. Travel medicine gives yellow fever vaccine. Which order is correct?

reference: "a single subcutaneous injection of 0.5 mL of reconstituted vaccine"; "YF-VAX is indicated for active immunization for the prevention of yellow fever in persons 9 months of age and older." Contraindicated with "a history of acute hypersensitivity to eggs or egg products due to a risk of anaphylaxis" and with severe immunosuppression including "thymic disease"; "Thymic disorders associated with abnormal immune cell function (e.g., myasthenia gravis, thymoma) may be an independent risk factor."

question: A 28-year-old healthcare worker with no eczema or atopic dermatitis (none currently and none at any time in the past), no other exfoliative skin condition, no immunosuppression, no known cardiac disease or multiple cardiac risk factors, and not pregnant, is enrolled in a first-responder pre-exposure program. She has no household contacts with eczematous conditions, immunosuppression, or pregnancy. Occupational health administers ACAM2000 by scarification at a single deltoid site with a bifurcated needle. Which technique is correct?

reference: "Rapidly make 15 jabs of the needle perpendicular to the skin through the vaccine droplet to puncture the skin, within a diameter of about 5 mm." (The same 15-jab procedure applies to primary vaccination and revaccination.)

question: A 34-year-old woman with cutaneous T-cell lymphoma (CTCL) refractory to at least one prior systemic therapy is not pregnant (negative pregnancy test within 1 week of starting), uses two reliable forms of contraception, and is not breastfeeding. She is not taking gemfibrozil. Baseline fasting triglycerides and TSH are normal and she has no known hypersensitivity to retinoids. Oncology initiates bexarotene. Which starting dose is correct?

reference: "The recommended initial dose of TARGRETIN is 300 mg/m2/day" taken "as a single oral daily dose with a meal." "The 300 mg/m2/day dose level of TARGRETIN may be adjusted to 200 mg/m2/day then to 100 mg/m2/day, or temporarily suspended, if necessitated by toxicity." "TARGRETIN must not be administered to a pregnant woman." "Concomitant administration of TARGRETIN and gemfibrozil is not recommended."

question: A 32-year-old woman with idiopathic pulmonary arterial hypertension (WHO Group 1; she does not have idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis) has been on ambrisentan 10 mg PO daily for 6 months. She is not pregnant: she is enrolled in the Letairis REMS with a documented negative pregnancy test this month and uses two acceptable forms of contraception. She has tolerated the drug well, with normal LFTs, no peripheral edema, and an improved 6-minute walk distance. PH specialist continues ambrisentan unchanged. Which ambrisentan regimen is appropriate?

choices.C: 5 mg PO daily + monthly pregnancy testing

reference: "Initiate treatment at 5 mg once daily... At 4-week intervals, either the dose of Letairis or tadalafil can be increased, as needed and tolerated, to Letairis 10 mg"; "Letairis is contraindicated in females who are pregnant"; "Letairis is contraindicated in patients with Idiopathic Pulmonary Fibrosis (IPF), including IPF patients with pulmonary hypertension (WHO Group 3)"

question: A 28-year-old woman with pulmonary arterial hypertension has been on macitentan 10 mg PO daily for 4 months. She is not pregnant: she is enrolled in the Opsumit REMS with a documented negative pregnancy test this month and uses two acceptable forms of contraception. She has no history of hypersensitivity to macitentan, and her hemoglobin and LFTs are normal. Specialist continues macitentan. Which regimen is appropriate?

reference: "The recommended dosage of OPSUMIT is 10 mg once daily for oral administration."; "Doses higher than 10 mg once daily have not been studied in patients with PAH and are not recommended."; "OPSUMIT is contraindicated in females who are pregnant."

question: A 34-year-old woman with chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension (CTEPH) that persists after pulmonary endarterectomy has been titrated over 10 weeks to riociguat 2.5 mg PO TID. She is not pregnant: she has a documented negative monthly pregnancy test, is enrolled in the Adempas REMS, and uses two acceptable forms of contraception. She takes no nitrate or nitric oxide donor, no PDE-5 inhibitor (specific or nonspecific), and no other soluble guanylate cyclase stimulator, and she does not have pulmonary hypertension associated with idiopathic interstitial pneumonia. reference: "The dose can be increased to the highest tolerated dosage, up to a maximum of 2.5 mg taken three times a day."; "If systolic blood pressure remains greater than 95 mmHg and the patient has no signs or symptoms of hypotension, up-titrate the dose by 0.5 mg taken three times a day."; "If at any time, the patient has symptoms of hypotension, decrease the dosage by 0.5 mg taken three times a day."; "Use of Adempas is contraindicated in patients who are pregnant"

question: A 51-year-old man with Child-Pugh B cirrhosis has had two episodes of overt hepatic encephalopathy in the past 6 months despite adherent lactulose therapy. He has no drug allergies and, specifically, no history of hypersensitivity to rifampin, rifabutin, rifapentine or any other rifamycin, and no prior exposure to rifaximin. GI starts rifaximin for reduction in the risk of overt HE recurrence. Which regimen is appropriate?

reference: "The recommended dosage of XIFAXAN is 550 mg taken orally two times a day." (hepatic encephalopathy); "The recommended dosage of XIFAXAN is 200 mg taken orally three times a day for 3 days." (travelers' diarrhea); "contraindicated in patients with a hypersensitivity to rifaximin, any of the rifamycin antimicrobial agents, or any of the components in XIFAXAN"

question: A 66-year-old man is 6 months post-MI and takes aspirin 81 mg daily. He has never had a stroke, a TIA or an intracranial hemorrhage, has no active pathological bleeding and no history of peptic ulcer disease, and has normal renal and hepatic function. Cardiology adds vorapaxar (Zontivity) for reduction of thrombotic cardiovascular events. Which regimen is appropriate?

choices.D: 2.08 mg PO daily × 12 mo then stop

reference: "Take one tablet of ZONTIVITY 2.08 mg orally once daily, with or without food."; "Use ZONTIVITY with aspirin and/or clopidogrel according to their indications or standard of care."; "ZONTIVITY is contraindicated in patients with a history of stroke, TIA, or ICH because of an increased risk of ICH in this population."; "ZONTIVITY is contraindicated in patients with active pathological bleeding such as ICH or peptic ulcer."

question: A 71-year-old man has just undergone PCI for NSTEMI. He has no history of intracranial hemorrhage, stroke or TIA, no active pathological bleeding, no hypersensitivity to ticagrelor, and normal hepatic function. He is not at high bleeding risk and the plan is 12 months of dual antiplatelet therapy. He has received a 180 mg ticagrelor loading dose and is on aspirin 81 mg daily. Cardiology continues ticagrelor. Which maintenance regimen is appropriate for the coming year?

choices.D: 90 mg PO BID × 6 mo then reassess

reference: "Initiate treatment with 180 mg oral loading dose of BRILINTA. question: A 34-year-old healthcare worker is offered vaccinia vaccine as first-responder pre-exposure prophylaxis. His wife completed chemotherapy for lymphoma 2 years ago, has been in sustained remission off all therapy since, and has a normal ANC of 4,200/µL. No one in the household is pregnant, under 1 year of age, immunocompromised, or affected by eczema or another exfoliative skin condition. reference: "Rapidly make 15 jabs of the needle perpendicular to the skin through the vaccine droplet"; "Do not administer ACAM2000 to individuals with severe immunodeficiency."

question: A 4-year-old boy with no chronic medical conditions attends an October vaccination visit. He has no asthma and no episode of wheezing in the past 12 months, is not immunocompromised, has no immunocompromised household contact requiring a protected environment, receives no aspirin or aspirin-containing therapy, and has had no severe allergic reaction to egg or to any previous influenza vaccine. question: A 44-year-old man with HIV is starting antiretroviral therapy. He has no cirrhosis and normal hepatic function (no Child-Pugh class B or C impairment), is hepatitis B and hepatitis C negative, drinks no alcohol, and has a CD4 count of 180 cells/mm3. choices.B: 200 mg PO daily indefinitely (no dose escalation)
choices.C: 100 mg PO daily × 14 d → 200 mg BID

reference: "The recommended dose for nevirapine is one 200 mg tablet daily for the first 14 days" "followed by one 200 mg tablet twice daily, in combination with other antiretroviral agents"; contraindicated in "Patients with moderate or severe (Child-Pugh Class B or C, respectively) hepatic impairment" and for "Use as part of occupational and non-occupational post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP) regimens"

question: A 62-year-old woman with metastatic breast cancer is DPYD wild-type on pharmacogenomic testing, with no dihydropyrimidine dehydrogenase deficiency. choices.A: 1250 mg/m² PO BID D1-14 per label

question: A 58-year-old man with invasive aspergillosis has been on voriconazole 200 mg PO BID for 3 weeks with clinical and radiographic improvement. His epilepsy is well controlled on levetiracetam 1000 mg PO BID.

question: A 68-year-old man with Parkinson disease on carbidopa/levodopa 25/100 four times daily and selegiline 5 mg PO BID has end-of-dose wearing off. Neurology adds entacapone.

choices.A: Selegiline 5 mg BID + entacapone 200 mg with each levodopa dose
choices.B: Selegiline 5 mg daily + entacapone 100 mg with each levodopa dose

question: A 62-year-old man with bipolar disorder maintained on divalproex sodium ER 1500 mg PO daily (valproate trough 92 mcg/mL) develops new hypertension at 152/94 mmHg with microalbuminuria. He takes no lithium. PCP starts lisinopril 20 mg PO daily.

choices.B: Divalproex ER 1000 mg + lisinopril 20 mg daily

question: A 68-year-old man on alfuzosin 10 mg XL PO daily for BPH develops invasive candidiasis with candidemia. He has no hepatic impairment. ID initiates micafungin 100 mg IV daily.

choices.A: Alfuzosin 10 mg XL + micafungin 100 mg IV daily

choices.C: Alfuzosin 2.5 mg XL + micafungin 100 mg IV daily

question: A 51-year-old man with HCV and HIV is on abacavir/dolutegravir/lamivudine (Triumeq) and has never taken efavirenz. choices.B: Zepatier 1 tab daily × 16 wk + continue dolutegravir-based ART

question: A 41-year-old woman on rilpivirine 25 mg PO daily as part of ART develops epilepsy. Neurology initiates levetiracetam 500 mg PO BID. She takes no acid-suppressing medication.

choices.B: Rilpivirine 50 mg daily + levetiracetam 500 mg BID

question: A 44-year-old man on etravirine 200 mg PO BID has epilepsy well controlled on levetiracetam 1000 mg PO BID and has been seizure-free for 2 years.

question: A 51-year-old man on Biktarvy 1 tab PO daily for HIV, with an undetectable viral load, has a positive IGRA on routine screening. He has no symptoms, and chest X-ray and sputum evaluation show no evidence of active tuberculosis. ID plans treatment for latent TB infection.

question: A 44-year-old woman on Biktarvy 1 tab PO daily has status epilepticus. Neurology loads levetiracetam 60 mg/kg IV, then continues levetiracetam 1000 mg PO BID.

question: A 71-year-old man had witnessed onset of left-sided weakness 8 hr ago. NIHSS has been 12 and unchanged over the past 4 hr on permissive hypertension. CTA shows a right M1 occlusion. question: A 51-year-old woman with symptomatic splenic marginal zone lymphoma is seen in pre-op clinic 21 d before her scheduled elective splenectomy. question: A 71-year-old man has taken metoprolol succinate ER 100 mg PO daily for 3 yr for hypertension. question: A 68-year-old woman awoke at 06:00 with right hemiparesis and aphasia; last known well 22:00 the prior evening. question: A 32-year-old G2P2 woman had a vaginal delivery 70 min ago with postpartum haemorrhage (EBL 1400 mL). She received IV TXA 1 g over 10 min at 40 min after delivery. reference: Early use of intravenous tranexamic acid (within 3 hours of birth) in addition to standard care is recommended for women with clinically diagnosed postpartum haemorrhage following vaginal birth or caesarean section. ... administration of tranexamic acid (TXA) at a fixed dose of 1 g (100 mg/mL) intravenously (IV) at 1 ml per minute (i.e. administered over 10 minutes), with a second dose of 1 g IV if bleeding continues after 30 minutes, or if bleeding restarts within 24 hours of completing the first dose.

question: A 68-year-old, 80 kg man on warfarin for atrial fibrillation has an INR of 3.2 and CT-confirmed perforated diverticulitis with peritonitis; laparotomy is booked within the hour. reference: KCENTRA, Prothrombin Complex Concentrate (Human), is a blood coagulation factor replacement product indicated for the urgent reversal of acquired coagulation factor deficiency induced by Vitamin K antagonist (VKA, e.g., warfarin) therapy in adult patients with: acute major bleeding or need for an urgent surgery/invasive procedure. ... question: A 32-year-old woman has a first episode of unilateral optic neuritis: pain on eye movement, a relative afferent pupillary defect, and Snellen acuity that has fallen to 20/200 over 3 d and is still worsening.
